prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1148; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in in Pasadena, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the best number to reach you.

A: I'd rather keep my name off the recording for now, but you can reach me through the claim file.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?

A: I was driving east on a two-lane road, going maybe twenty-five miles an hour. Traffic was light. The other car came toward me from the opposite direction and drifted into my lane.

Q: Did you have time to react?

A: Barely. I braked and turned slightly to the right, but we still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, more of a jolt, but my airbags didn't deploy.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?

A: Yes, I walked around for a few minutes. I felt stiff, but I didn't think much of it at the time.

Q: Have you noticed any injuries since then?

A: Yes. My neck is sore, especially when I turn my head to the left, and my lower back has an ache that gets worse after I sit for a while. I saw a doctor who diagnosed a neck and back strain and gave me some muscle relaxers and a referral for physical therapy.

Q: Are you currently receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I'm going to physical therapy twice a week, and I'm trying to keep up with the home exercises they gave me.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get back to normal.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
